## Reading the ratings

These are **player-only lineup ratings**: one coefficient for each player, with
controls for the toss and batting first. The five-year window averages performance
across that period. It includes retired players and does not claim to measure
instantaneous form. Scores can be compared within each table, but not between
formats or men's and women's competitions.

The predictor adds the eleven player coefficients on one side and subtracts those
on the other. Replacing player $j$ with player $i$ changes the predictor by
$\beta_i-\beta_j$. A difference of 0.2 multiplies modeled win/loss odds by
$\exp(0.2)\approx1.22$. In a binary match model, moving from 50% win probability
would then mean about 55%. In Tests this comparison conditions on a decisive
result; the model separately predicts draws.

Cross-team matches connect the ratings. Stable teammate combinations still make
individual attribution difficult, and omitted team conditions can be assigned to
players. Regularization supplies a particular allocation of shared performance.
The CSVs identify players with identical participation patterns, appearance counts,
and each player's largest teammate-overlap share. A connected schedule alone does
not establish that every player's contribution is separately identified.

The Test model retains draws and ties in a symmetric three-outcome model with a
common draw propensity. Weather and playing conditions are not modeled separately.
ODI and T20I tables use decisive matches. All formats require unambiguous fixed XIs;
recorded match replacements are excluded. Cricsheet coverage is incomplete and
currently withholds some Afghanistan-related matches. Counts, exclusions, source
hashes, tuning scores, and fitted coefficients are included with the publication.

These point estimates do not have rank intervals and are **not wins above
replacement**. Sorting them does not remove uncertainty in attribution. See the
[format-ranking specification](format_rankings.qmd) for the estimator, tuning rules,
and checks, and the [ODI forecast comparison](models.qmd) for the earlier
out-of-sample experiment. The final-year scores used to select regularization in
these new fits are tuning results, not an independent evaluation.

## Earlier ODI experiment

The [historical ODI rankings](../out/release/lineup/rankings.csv) retain the saved
2023–2025 fit cutoffs, team-plus-player and player-only variants, and three- and
five-year windows. They are separate from the new format tables. The original
[experiment specification](lineup_experiment.qmd) and saved analysis remain intact;
the user-requested ranking extensions are documented separately.
